minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee held a special meeting to conduct a 75-minute, 13-question finalist interview for superintendent with candidate Timothy McCormack, currently superintendent in North Brookfield. Questions covered his background, budget philosophy, hiring practices, student safety, staff culture, labor relations, a past personal-conduct disclosure, and handling of a Facebook controversy over a Turkey Hill hire; the meeting ended with McCormack's closing statement and a roll-call vote to adjourn, with no hiring decision made.

what_happened.line: School Committee interviewed superintendent finalist Timothy McCormack in a 75-minute, 13-question session; no hiring decision was made.
McCormack discussed reconciling new programs with a recent budget cut and outlined grant funding for career-pathway programs.
He described state aid pressures in his current district, including a rural aid reduction not fully offset by Chapter 70.
McCormack disclosed and answered questions about a past personal-conduct matter from a prior district, which was investigated internally and externally.
He was asked how he handled online backlash over a hiring decision at a local business.

why_it_matters: The Committee is choosing who will run the district's budget and staffing decisions going forward; his answers on cuts, grants, and state aid speak to how he'd manage the town's school appropriation.
The personal-conduct disclosure and the hiring-backlash question bear on how he handles judgment calls and public scrutiny in the role.
No vote was taken on hiring; residents should watch for when and how the Committee decides among finalists.
